title: Mullvad VPN After One Year: The Honest Review
creator: Kai Brenner
description:
I've used Mullvad as my only VPN for twelve months. I paid for it myself, every month, with my own money. Nobody sent me anything and nobody saw this video before you.

sentences.t: A year ago I cancelled every VPN subscription I had and moved everything over to Mullvad.
Not because anyone paid me to, nobody did, but because I was sick of VPN marketing.
So this is twelve months of actually living with it, the good stuff and the stuff that drives me up the wall.
Let's start with the thing that makes Mullvad weird, which is how you sign up.
You don't give it an email, you don't make a password, you don't even give it a name.
You press a button and it hands you a sixteen digit account number, and that's your whole identity.
Lose the number, lose the account, there's no forgot password link to save you.
I wrote mine on a sticky note inside a cookbook, which my partner thinks is insane.
And then there's the price, which is the part that genuinely surprised me.
Mullvad costs five euros a month, flat, and that's it.
There's no two year deal, there's no seventy percent off, there's no countdown timer on the checkout page.
You can pay Mullvad by card, but you can also literally mail them cash in an envelope with your account number on a slip of paper.
I tried it, I sent them a ten euro note from a post office, and about a week later Mullvad added two months to my account.
Compare that to most of the industry, where the price on the banner and the price on renewal are two very different numbers.
Okay, speed, because that's what most of you will actually care about.
I ran tests every week from my flat in Hamburg on a five hundred megabit line.
On WireGuard to a server in Germany I lose maybe ten percent, which I honestly never notice.
To New York it drops to around two hundred, which is still more than enough for streaming.
Over OpenVPN it's slower, noticeably slower, so I just don't use it.
Streaming is where it gets messy, though, and I want to be upfront about that.
Mullvad does not try to unblock streaming catalogs, they say so themselves, it's not what they're for.
Some days the American Netflix library loaded, most days it didn't, and that's on purpose.
If watching other countries' shows is your main reason for a VPN, this is probably the wrong tool.
Now, the stuff that annoys me.
They removed port forwarding a while back, which broke a couple of things I used for self hosting.
The app on my phone sometimes forgets it was connected after a reboot, and I've caught it off more than once.
And there's no browser extension that just works the way the other big names do, you either run the app or you don't.
Also the server list is smaller, which is fine for me, but if you need some tiny country, check before you pay.
On privacy, which is the whole point, the track record is honestly pretty great.
The Swedish police showed up at their office with a warrant once and left with nothing, because there was nothing to take.
That story is the reason I trust them more than any audit badge on a homepage.
So, verdict after a year.
If you want a VPN for privacy and you hate being upsold, Mullvad is the one I'd tell a friend about.
If you want to unlock streaming libraries, look somewhere else, and that's fine.
I'm keeping it, I'm paying for year two out of my own pocket, and I'll check back if anything changes.
Let me know what you use in the comments, and thanks for watching.
